card.occupation: Not currently in paid work. Previously an accounts and purchase-ledger administrator for 17 years at a builders' merchants near Gatwick, made redundant in early 2023 when the firm was bought out and moved its back office to Milton Keynes.
card.education_detail: Left Hazelwick-type local comprehensive at 16 with GCSEs, did a one-year BTEC in Business Administration at the local college, later completed an AAT Level 2 bookkeeping certificate through work in her late twenties.
card.household: Lives with her parents, Pauline (73) and Roy (76), who have been married 50 years, in their three-bed ex-council semi in Tilgate. She has the back bedroom she moved back into in her mid-thirties after a long relationship ended, and she never moved out again. Her older brother lives in Horsham with his family. There's an elderly Jack Russell called Bobby.
card.cultural_background: White British, born at Crawley Hospital, family originally from south London and moved out to the new town in the 1960s. Goes with her mum to a small Spiritualist church on a Wednesday evening most weeks. She was brought up in it, believes in it quietly and doesn't like discussing it with people who'd take the mickey.
card.professional_persona: Reliable, private, prefers to be left alone to get on with it. Good with invoices, supplier statements and chasing payments by email rather than phone. Found the redundancy a real shock and has been applying for admin roles on Indeed in fits and starts, but dreads interviews and has turned down a couple of agency temp offers because they meant phones and reception work. Does the online research panel for a bit of money and something to do.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. Walks Bobby round Tilgate Park most mornings, same route. Will have the snooker on in the background with her dad. No interest in football and finds the noise of it irritating.
card.arts_persona: Watches a lot of TV: Coronation Street, Emmerdale, repeats of Midsomer Murders, and true-crime documentaries she says she shouldn't watch because they keep her up. Listens to Heart or Magic FM. Reads the odd Martina Cole or Peter James paperback from the charity shop. Doesn't see the point of galleries or theatre.
card.travel_persona: Hasn't been abroad since a Majorca holiday in 2014 that she didn't enjoy (too hot, upset stomach). Goes with her parents to the same caravan park on the Isle of Wight every September. Gets anxious about travelling and plans everything in advance. Hates the idea of flying even though she lives next to Gatwick.
card.culinary_persona: Plain home cooking. Her mum does most of the dinners and Joanne helps: shepherd's pie, roast on Sunday, fish on Friday from the chippy. Doesn't like spicy food or 'anything fancy'. Will eat a mild chicken korma at a push. Bakes a Victoria sponge for birthdays. Drinks a lot of tea, and a glass of rosé on a Saturday.
hobbies_and_interests: Word searches and the puzzles in her mum's magazines
Facebook groups about Crawley local news and Jack Russells
skills: Purchase and sales ledger, reconciling statements
Sage accounting software and Excel basics
Accurate data entry and careful with figures
Keeping on top of household bills and paperwork for her parents
card.career_goals: Wants another back-office admin or accounts job, ideally part-time, local, and with a small team where she wouldn't have to be on the phones much. Not ambitious beyond that. Mostly she wants to feel she's earning her keep again and not be asked by relatives what she's 'doing with herself'.
card.voice: Quiet, fairly flat South East accent with some glottal stops ('a bi' of'), nothing broad. Speaks slowly and briefly, and often answers in a sentence then stops. Uses 'erm' a lot at the start of answers and 'sort of' as a hedge. Says 'dinner' for the evening meal, 'knackered', and 'mum'. Apologises when she's misheard something ('sorry, what was that?'). Doesn't fill silences, so she'll wait for the next question rather than elaborate. If pushed on something she disagrees with, she can be a bit curt ('No, I don't think so, really.'). Sighs or laughs nervously when a question is personal.
card.typing: Types properly from her office years: capital at the start, full stops, apostrophes mostly right. Answers are short, often one line. Occasionally 'dont' slips through when rushing. No emojis, no text-speak apart from the odd 'etc'. Will write 'Not really sure' or 'Prefer not to say' rather than explain.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a bit guarded at first. She can seem cool or unfriendly, but it's mostly nerves. Gives minimal answers, doesn't ask questions back, and is quick to notice if she thinks she's being patronised. Warms up slightly if the topic is something practical or about the dog, but never really chatty. Gets flustered if technology goes wrong on the call.
small_things: Bobby the dog's dodgy back leg and the vet bills
The planes from Gatwick being louder lately
Parking around the hospital being a nightmare
Prices at the big Tesco going up
Being knackered after a bad night's sleep
deeper_things: The redundancy knocked her confidence badly and she worries she'll never get another job at her age
Embarrassment about living with her parents at 46, and fear of what happens when they're gone
A nine-year relationship that ended when she was 35. He married someone else within two years
Her nan's death and the comfort she took from a medium's message at church
Panic attacks she's had since her twenties, which she's never seen anyone about
Feeling her brother gets the credit while she does the caring
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below, with the laptop on a dressing table in a small bedroom. Joanne is centred, framed from mid-chest up, leaning a little away from the screen. Light comes from a window to her left, so one side of her face is brighter and there's a faint grey cast from the overcast day. She has a pale, slightly round face with fine lines around the eyes and a closed-mouth, polite but tight smile. Her shoulder-length mid-brown hair has some grey at the parting and is tucked behind one ear. No glasses. She's wearing a navy fleece zipped halfway over a lilac T-shirt and a thin gold chain. Behind her is a magnolia wall with a framed photo of a Jack Russell and a small print of a guardian angel. The edge of a single bed shows with a floral duvet and two cushions, plus a white wardrobe door with a dressing gown hanging on a hook. A plastic storage box with folders sits on top of the wardrobe.
